sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Sevier County?
sections.html:
Three offices share the work, and all of them sit in the Sevier County Courthouse at 125 Court Avenue in Sevierville. The Property Assessor values the land and buildings, the County Commission picks the rate, and the Trustee sends the bills and takes the money. Knowing which desk answers which question saves a lot of walking between floors.

  • Property Assessor: Suite 210 West, voice 865.453.3242, open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The office appraises, classifies and assesses taxable property and updates ownership and tax maps from recorded deeds.
  • Trustee: Room 212W, telephone (865) 453-2767, same weekday hours. It is the first office on the right inside the west-end doors. A drop box for payments sits behind the courthouse at the entrance to the 30 minute parking area off West Bruce Street.
  • Clerk and Master: Suite 108 W, (865) 453-4654. This is the office that collects delinquent taxes in Chancery Court and runs the tax sale auction.

The county's Property Assessor page stresses that the Assessor does not set the rate. Sevier County also contains the cities of Sevierville, Pigeon Forge and Gatlinburg, so ask the city hall where the house stands whether a separate city bill applies.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Sevier County for a home seller?
sections.html:
Sevier County covers 598 square miles at the foot of the Great Smoky Mountains, with Sevierville as the county seat and largest city. About thirty percent of the Great Smoky Mountains National Park lies inside the county line, and tourism is the engine of the local economy. Gatlinburg and Pigeon Forge draw visitors to Ripley's Aquarium of the Smokies, Ober Gatlinburg and Dollywood, and the cabin rental industry has grown with them. One school district, Sevier County Schools, serves the whole county.

That visitor traffic matters on the tax side, because the Assessor runs an online filing for nightly rentals and the county publishes a short-term rental tax estimator beside its primary home and vacant land estimator. Census Bureau QuickFacts for Sevier County lists:

  • 101,342 residents on July 1, 2025, up 2.7% from the April 2020 base
  • 62,724 housing units, with 70.7% of occupied homes owner-occupied (2020 to 2024)
  • $299,000 median value for an owner-occupied home
  • $62,581 median household income and a 13.2% poverty rate
  • 1,139 building permits issued in 2025

sections.h2: How is a Sevier County property tax bill figured?
sections.html:
Tennessee multiplies the appraised value by a state-set ratio and then by the local rate. The State Comptroller's tax bill guide sets residential and farm property at 25 percent of appraised value and commercial or industrial property at 40 percent. The rate is quoted per $100 of assessed value.

A worked example: a house appraised at $300,000 carries an assessed value of $75,000. The Trustee's FAQ gives $1.48 per $100 for 2024, which would produce $1,110 for the year. Treat that as an illustration only. Sevier County reappraises every five years, and 2026 is a reappraisal year. The county's statement on reappraisal notices says the Assessor must review roughly 90,000 parcels, that state law then requires a certified rate meant to keep total collections level, and that the Board of Commissioners adopts the final rate. Some owners will pay more than before and some less, so look at the 2026 bill itself.

Between reappraisals, values stay put unless the property changes physically. A sale alone does not change the assessment.

sections.h2: When is Sevier County property tax due, and where are we in the calendar?
sections.html:
The 2026 bills went out in early October, and they can be paid from October 1 through the last day of February 2027 without interest. Today is November 15, 2026, so the account is in its open payment window. Interest of 1.5 percent a month starts on March 1, 2027 for anything unpaid. Mailed payments need a postmark by the deadline, since the Trustee does not accept an office meter date, and online payments count on the day of the transaction. Partial payments are accepted, and the unpaid balance is what collects interest.

Sevier County property tax calendar (Property Assessor and Trustee pages)
DateWhat happens
January 1Assessment date for ownership, assessments and tax maps
March 1Business personal property schedules due; greenbelt applications due
MayAssessment change notices mailed
June 1County Board of Equalization starts hearing appeals
First week of OctoberTrustee mails bills; payable from October 1

Mortgage companies do not receive a copy from the Trustee, so an owner with an escrow account should forward the bill. The year's tax covers the current calendar year.

sections.h2: How do I dispute a Sevier County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the Assessor, then go to the County Board of Equalization if the answer is unsatisfactory. The county's reappraisal statement lists the Assessor's reappraisal line at (865) 774-3756, weekdays 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the email address reappraisal@seviercountytn.gov. It also tells owners who think the value is wrong that they may file an appeal with the Board of Equalization, which begins hearing appeals on June 1.

Gather evidence before you call: recent sales of similar houses, repair estimates for defects the appraisal missed, and any facts about square footage or condition. Ask the Assessor's office for the current-year filing deadline, because the notice date changes with each cycle. Do not wait for the bill to arrive before you start.

sections.h2: What property tax relief is available in Sevier County?
sections.html:
The Trustee runs two state programs for homeowners, and staff fill out the application with you in person. Tax Relief pays all or part of the tax on a home, including a mobile home, for owners who are 65 or older, disabled, a disabled veteran, or the widow or widower of a disabled veteran. The posted figures for 2025 taxes were:

  • Elderly and disabled owners: income limit of $37,530 including a spouse, with relief calculated on a market value up to $32,700
  • Disabled veterans and their surviving spouses: no income test, with relief calculated on a market value up to $175,000
  • Tax Freeze for owners 65 or older: income cannot exceed $47,990 for 2024, and the application is renewed every year

Relief also covers city taxes. Greenbelt is a separate break for property of 15 acres or more in farm or forestry use, applied for by March 1. Land that leaves the program owes a rollback of the taxes saved over the last three years. Ask the Trustee for the limits that apply to your current year before you plan around these numbers.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Sevier County tax when I sell?
sections.html:
The lien stays with the parcel, so unpaid tax must be cleared at or before closing. The Trustee mails the bill to the owner of record, and its FAQ advises new owners to read the closing statement to see who handles the year's tax. A title company normally pays any balance from the sale proceeds.

If a bill goes unpaid past the end of February, the account turns delinquent. Delinquent accounts are handed to Chancery Court, where costs are added and the parcel can be advertised for the annual auction. The Clerk and Master lists properties 20 to 30 days before the sale in the Mountain Press, bidders must register in person 30 minutes before the sale, and payment is cash, money order or check. The owner has one year to redeem, and the buyer earns 1 percent a month during that period. Anyone with a delinquent account should call the Trustee at (865) 453-2767 before the auction list is published.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Sevier County?
faqs.a: The Sevier County Trustee mails it, usually in the first week of October. The Assessor sets the value and the County Commission sets the rate, but only the Trustee at 125 Court Avenue, Room 212W, collects payment. Call (865) 453-2767 if a bill does not arrive.

faqs.q: What is the last day to pay Sevier County property tax without interest?
faqs.a: The last day of February. For the 2026 bill that means February 2027. From March 1, interest of 1.5 percent a month (18 percent a year) is added, and a late postmark counts as a late payment.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Sevier County taxes in installments?
faqs.a: Partial payments are accepted at the Trustee's office. Whatever remains unpaid when the account turns delinquent collects interest. Older owners may also qualify for the state Tax Relief or Tax Freeze programs, which the Trustee administers in person.

faqs.q: How often does Sevier County reappraise property?
faqs.a: Every five years, and 2026 is a reappraisal year. The Assessor's page says values hold between cycles unless the property physically changes. After a reappraisal, the state process produces a certified rate designed to keep collections steady.

faqs.q: Does an unpaid Sevier County tax bill block a sale?
faqs.a: It does not block the sale, but it must be paid from the proceeds, because the lien follows the parcel. Ask the Trustee for the payoff amount for the closing date. Tax accounts that go to Chancery Court carry added costs and can end in a tax sale.
